Construction Mafia

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A series of attacks on construction projects by AK-47-wielding thugs known as the ‘construction mafia’ are crippling the economy under the guise of radial economic transformation.

Unique Selling Point:
- SEXY CRIME TREND IMPACTING ON ECONOMY
- FOOTAGE OF ACTUAL INTIMIDATION, THREATS & DEMANDS

Summary:
Corporate South Africa is under siege. Businesses are engulfed in wave after wave of illegal protest action often marred by violence, harm and the destruction of property.

Construction sites across the country are brought to halt by local communities claiming to be Business Forums that demand their cut in projects – be it in the form of employment, sub-contracting or in some cases straight up cash.

We investigate this alarming trend and the impact it has on the country’s economy.

Further information:
WHAT’s THE STORY
The so-called construction mafia has been disrupting construction projects countrywide, demanding that 30% of the project value be awarded to local companies. In some instances the groups, calling themselves business forums, seek control of the full 30%, with the aim of distributing jobs and contracts among local workers and business people themselves. But their demands are not always so idealistic – they want cash to go away.

IT’s SPREADING ACROSS SA
After leading a campaign of terror for many years in KwaZulu-Natal, have infiltrated Gauteng and laid siege to construction projects and mining companies all over the province and surrounding areas.

FINANCIAL IMPACT
The financial impact of these protests is catastrophic – no business can sustain the continuous onslaught of work stoppages, delays in completing works, threats and intimidation to management, and employees living in constant fear of their lives.
In 2019 the construction mafia had disrupted and halted at least 78 projects worth a minimum of R25.5 billion.

Illegal site disruptions caused listed construction and engineering group Aveng and European-based Strabag International to withdraw from an SA National Roads Agency (Sanral) project that forms part of the N2 Wild Coast Road Construction project, over fears for the safety of their employees.

Armed gangs in March last year also halted construction on the R2.4 billion German oil storage investment project being built in Saldanha by JSE-listed construction group WBHO.

THE MAFIA MO
A mob of protestors is mobilised to demonstrate outside a construction site based on a concocted grievance mostly along the lines that the private company has flouted its statutory obligations – in other words, unproven allegations that the company hired labour or appointing sub-contractors from outside the local community.

They get violent, they threaten staff and in some cases they resort to straight up extortion.

WHO IS THIS MAFIA?
The mob representatives pass themselves off as the (self-appointed) local chapter of a ‘business forum’, or community.

FEDERATION FOR RADICAL ECONOMIC TRANSFORMATION (FFRET)
FFRET represents at least 37 business forums which reportedly has more than 3 000 members. The organisation’s leader Malusi Zondi acknowledged to that most of these members are former criminals to other journalists.

Zondi has said Ffret is working to professionalise the members and is organising itself in all provinces, adding that members shut down construction sites because they were robbed of their “fair share” (by contractors).

NATIONAL TREASURY
The situation had arisen due to local communities misunderstanding a National Treasury regulation about subcontracting that was implemented in April 2017.

The Preferential Procurement Policy Framework Act, 5 of 2000 (PPPFA) requires, inter alia, bidders of projects to the value of R30 million or more to sub-contract at least 30% of the value of the contract to exempted micro enterprises (EMEs) or qualifying small business enterprises (QSEs) or a small business as defined in the National Small Business Act, 1996.

The PPPFA applies to public enterprise (organs of state) only, and not to private business. There is no statutory obligation for a private business to allocate 30% of its works to contractors from the local area. There is no legal basis underpinning the protestors’ grievance.

Treasury warned that organs of state that are using procurement preferences not provided for in the regulatory framework – including ring-fencing contracts for service providers and suppliers who live in a certain geographical area – are non-compliant and that such expenditure will be classified as having been irregularly incurred.

THE PRESIDENT’s TAKE ON IT
In 2018 Ramaphosa weighed in on the matter, the SABC reported. He was addressing business leaders in Pietermartizburg

Ramaphosa referred to people who are hijacking policies and distorting radical economic transformation by disrupting sites and demanding 30% of the value of projects, describing these practices as “radical economic robbery” and calling for consequences.

NOT JUST REGULAR CRIME
The NPA agreed that the disruption of construction sites should not be dealt with as just a common criminal act but in terms of the Prevention of Organised Crime Act. SAPS have launched a dedicated unit under the Anti-Gang sector of Organised Crime in Gauteng to focus on these incidents.

WHAT WE HAVE
- We have videos of disruptions, threats of violence and demands made by the so-called construction mafia
- We’ll have access to some these sites where there is current disruptions
- We’re trying to get a specific person to confront who has been demanding cash

INTERVIEWS
- SA Forum of Civil Engineering Contractors (Safcec) CEO Webster Mfebe
- Karen de Beer – Medium Size Contractor
- Malusi Zondi – Federations for Radical Economic Transformation
- Jas XXX – Security Contractor protecting sites
- Informant – giving insight into the business forums
- SAPS or LEGAL EXPERT – ACTING UNLAWFULLY, misunderstanding of National Treasury Regulation.
- Confront with dodgy Business Forum

Press Release:


The Construction Mafia
They’re known as the Construction Mafia – community groups who demand a cut in building projects around the country, sometimes even resorting to violence and intimidation to get their way. From some form of employment, sub-contracting to their small businesses or in some cases straight up cash – they say they’ll continue to hold construction sites to ransom until they receive their share. Carte Blanche investigates.
Producer: Nicky Troll | Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli


Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: South Africa’s construction industry is worth Billions of rands every year – employing thousands of people and contributing to the development of the country.

LINK: But this sector is under threat. The so-called construction mafia is holding contractors to ransom demanding employment, cash and halting projects – even is it means intimidating contractors, damaging property and getting violent.

UPSOUND CLIP OF SOME CHAOS – THINK THE BULLDOZER ONE….

VO: Groups claiming to be Business Forums rock up at construction projects – they will strong arm their way onto the site and forcefully disrupt operations.

It’s an alarming trend that even President Cyril Ramposa has raised concerns about, as far back as 2018.

PRESIDENT: “that is not radical economic transformation, that is radical economic robbery – and we can not allow that”

WEBSTER: They are weaponized. Organized. People. // use extortionate methods To achieve compliance with their needs that are not in line with the law.

VO: Webster Mfebe from the South African Forum of Civil Engineering Contractors – he says the industry is powerless against this criminality.

WEBSTER: We are trained to build that infrastructure//. //The industry is not trained on warfare.

VO: The current tension stems from what appears to be a misunderstanding of a National Treasury regulation related to subcontracting.

The Preferential Procurement Regulations of 2017, requires bidders of projects to contract a portion of the development to small businesses in local communities, specifically black owned businesses.

LINK: 30% of projects over R30 million should go to local contractors - BUT it applies to government projects and NOT the private sector.

VO: Yet the private construction sector is being targeted on a daily basis across the country. Karen de Beer owns a medium construction business – and has experienced the wrath of the construction mafia on her sites.

MAC: Karen, have you ever had a point where you have to close your site for a day.
KAREN: Not for a day not for a week for months.

VO: Karen is beyond frustrated - It now takes almost double the time to complete projects because of disruptions at the hands of volitile groups masquerading as business forums.

KAREN: // They come in they run 100 of them you can't control so many people and they just break down the walls that you have just built

PETER: // This is unfortunately starting to become a South African model of doing business. …. It’s working

VO: The damage to the economy is severe and the consequences are far reaching explains legal expert Peter Barnard.

PETER: if their demands aren't met. Individuals will be hurt, the plant and the project will suffer, be burned, damaged, destroyed or they will simply ensure that no further work continues

WEBSTER: // the projects that are being disrupted are around 42 billion rand - an issue which would have been a state of emergency if it was in other countries in advanced economies.

VO: While court interdicts offer some relief to contractors, it’s not a cure all.

Amongst the affected projects were two major contracts worth billions of rands that were awarded to listed companies.

The Sanral N2 Wild Coast Road Construction project in the Eastern Cape was eventually abandoned over fears for the safety of their employees.

While a German oil storage investment project in Saldanha Bay suffered R75 million rands worth of damage to equipment and structures at the hands of so-called business forums in a matter of hours.

WEBSTER: When the police arrive on time, watched the property being torched, watch the employees running in the veld…. Not trained to deal with public violence.

VO: The police’s seeming reluctance to deal with these cases at station level appears to be a national trend – combating this crime will require high level police intervention explains Barnard.

PETER: // the way in which the conduct is carried out is basic thuggery. But there is a method to this madness. This is organised and it's getting worse MULTI2 M3

VO: We came across one of these Business Forums in Brooklyn Pretoria. They were aggressive from the moment we arrived.

UPSOUND SHOUTING

VO: Eventually, the man claiming to be in charge Mafika Mhlangu agreed to an interview. He says he represents Military Veterans from the wider Pretoria area.

UPSOUND CONFRONT 30%
MAC – processes
….this guy not the owner of the project.”

VO: Jas Smit is a security consultant for the Brooklyn development.

JAS: It's a private owned land to private development. the developers are basically put at a choice of either continuing under the demands of these groups or work at a loss.

VO: The group is adamant they want their share of the profits and say they will take matters into their own hands.

UPSOUND CONFRONT: WE ask him to give us the bill of quantities ….. we close the site down.

VO: The construction mafia knows no boundaries explains Roy Mnisi from Master Builders South Africa.

ROY: You cannot go to a construction site and start demanding books, bills of quantities and so forth. You don't do that. That's not how it works. // that it's mafia tendencies that to be speaking about that is not acceptable at all. M27

VO: But the group insisted they were with in their rights.

UPSOUND – any project – 30% should be givne
MAC: government
.... government & public.

PETER: I'm afraid that's not correct. You've got private sector and you’ve got public sector. private sector // you can hire whoever you want. There is nothing regulating that. In public sector. There are specific laws and regulations which deal with how government has to procure those services

VO: When we tried to clarify this point – the group turned on us.

UPSOUND CONFRONT – CHASING

LINK: MAC LEAVING SITE…. I can’t

VO: Shortly after we left with our cameras – the men forced their way onto the site and demanded that workers down tools.

The Federation for Radical Economic Transformation represents a number of business forums nationwide. Spokesperson Sifiso Shezi claims the Federation is making a positive impact in bridging the divide between their members and contractors.

SIFISO: our forums affiliate to us they've got a constitution. They are registered and therefore anything else that calls itself forum outside of that we we we we distance ourselves from them

VO: While Shezi admits there’s been trial and error to their approach in the past, he insists the federation’s members are not thugs.

MAC: I as an ordinary citizen was scared for my life.
SIFISO: Well it's an isolated incident. And most of them there that are taking that shape I guess they fear they fall outside of the scope of our mandate. It's an element that // we need to isolate it and condemn it with all contempt that it deserves.

VO: It is by no means an isolated incident. This is daily reality for contractors all over the country confirmed Mnisi.

ROY: // in many areas that we experience these mafia tendencies. The contractors are black contractors the main contractors and subcontractors all black contractors. M28

VO: In some cases, the exploitation even extends to the very people they claim to represent explains Barnard.

PETER: // when these forums come along they then take a cut or a percentage of the money that's generated meaning that the actual humans on site doing the work end up by earning less than they would have earned if they'd been employed directly. M6

VO: Shezi argues, forums are not unions and are there to make money.

SIFISO: // just because it's black business it doesn't mean now we must we must take care off of the social element of the economy. We are there not to make money like every other business and we are not saying we we are not apologetic it's a capitalist system // M30

VO: Some forums have even taken it a step further – they don’t want jobs, they’ll simply settle for cold hard cash.

UPSOUND CELLPHONE CLIPS – ASK FOR MONEY….peacefully.

JAS: // it's either protection money or buyout and then they say well we'll leave your site and you can work with who you want and we won't bother you.
MAC: What kind of money are we talking about.
JAS Well anything from a few thousand to hundreds of thousands at one time M14

KAREN: // I mean the moment that you pay any of them back you are done. I mean I refused to pay protection money because otherwise how can I work M31

VO: It seems to be a lucrative income stream – with these rogue business forums even going up against each other.

ROY: // even if you were to give them their demands tomorrow, another one comes and say OK you contracted with that one. It's not part of us. We are independent from them. You have to contract with us. It can't work and it's not working at all.M29

VO: Shezi also doesn’t feel things are working – he believes the current legislation simply cannot effectively address economic transformation – it needs to include the private sector too.

SIFISO: // We need to be cognizant of the imbalances of the past // we are talking about people that have been colonized for centuries. People that have been given a certain type of education and all of a sudden you come and say we voted. We are equal. We can never be equal. Hence the that the legislation of 30 percent participation in government is not sufficient to transform the economy. MULTI2 M6

LINK: //CUT calling it economic transformation doesn’t justify thuggery… it’s criminal behavior that costs the country billions of rands in losses and negatively impacts on international investor perceptions – this is economic sabotage.

WEBSTER: All these cases where the violently disrupt and over 2 billion Brain Project. [from middle of clip]// You cannot equate it to. A boy who has stolen a bar of chocolate in a supermarket // You need to deal with this matter should the prevention of organized crime // M15

VO: President Ramaposa promised action in his 2020 State of the Nation Address.
UPSOUND SONA:
“I have prioritised our response to the growing problem of criminal groups that extort money from construction and other businesses. Specialised units – bringing together SAPS and the National Prosecuting Authority – are mandated to combat these crimes of economic disruption. “

VO: While all parties agree that economic transformation is necessary, the execution is problematic and these disruptions are not ecomically sustainable.

PETER: We can't have South African business growing at gunpointM8// If the will of the people is that there's not enough being done in the industry. Construction specifically for radical economic transformation. Then there has to be dealt with by the legislature.

ROY: if we don't deal with this problem I am afraid we will see the collapse of the construction industry in South Africa. //. M17 // M18 // we will continue to see many people losing their jobs as a result of this so-called construction mafia //


PROMO 1
VO: A series of attacks on construction projects by violent thugs known as the Construction Mafia, cripple the economy under the guise of radical economic transformation – costing the country billions.

PROMO 2
VO: Construction sites are disrupted by so-called business forums demanding their cut in projects - they violently threaten workers and ruthlessly damage propety – is this economic transformation or mafia tactics at work?

PROMO 3
VO: They’re known as the Construction Mafia – so-called businness forums brazenly intimidate and violently threaten construction companies around the country, demanding a cut of the profits.

It’s working VO: The damage to the economy is severe and the consequences are far reaching explains legal expert Peter Barnard. PETER: if their demands aren't met. Individuals will be hurt, the plant and the project will suffer, be burned, damaged, destroyed or they will simply ensure that no further work continues WEBSTER: // the projects that are being disrupted are around 42 billion rand - an issue which would have been a state of emergency if it was in other countries in advanced economies. VO: While court interdicts offer some relief to contractors, it’s not a cure all. Amongst the affected projects were two major contracts worth billions of rands that were awarded to listed companies. The Sanral N2 Wild Coast Road Construction project in the Eastern Cape was eventually abandoned over fears for the safety of their employees. While a German oil storage investment project in Saldanha Bay suffered R75 million rands worth of damage to equipment and structures at the hands of so-called business forums in a matter of hours. WEBSTER: When the police arrive on time, watched the property being torched, watch the employees running in the veld…. Not trained to deal with public violence. VO: The police’s seeming reluctance to deal with these cases at station level appears to be a national trend – combating this crime will require high level police intervention explains Barnard. PETER: // the way in which the conduct is carried out is basic thuggery. But there is a method to this madness. This is organised and it's getting worse MULTI2 M3 VO: We came across one of these Business Forums in Brooklyn Pretoria. They were aggressive from the moment we arrived. UPSOUND SHOUTING VO: Eventually, the man claiming to be in charge Mafika Mhlangu agreed to an interview. He says he represents Military Veterans from the wider Pretoria area. UPSOUND CONFRONT 30% MAC – processes ….this guy not the owner of the project.” VO: Jas Smit is a security consultant for the Brooklyn development. JAS: It's a private owned land to private development. the developers are basically put at a choice of either continuing under the demands of these groups or work at a loss. VO: The group is adamant they want their share of the profits and say they will take matters into their own hands. UPSOUND CONFRONT: WE ask him to give us the bill of quantities ….. we close the site down. VO: The construction mafia knows no boundaries explains Roy Mnisi from Master Builders South Africa. ROY: You cannot go to a construction site and start demanding books, bills of quantities and so forth. You don't do that. That's not how it works. // that it's mafia tendencies that to be speaking about that is not acceptable at all. M27 VO: But the group insisted they were with in their rights. UPSOUND – any project – 30% should be givne MAC: government .... government & public. PETER: I'm afraid that's not correct. You've got private sector and you’ve got public sector. private sector // you can hire whoever you want. There is nothing regulating that. In public sector. There are specific laws and regulations which deal with how government has to procure those services VO: When we tried to clarify this point – the group turned on us. UPSOUND CONFRONT – CHASING LINK: MAC LEAVING SITE…. I can’t VO: Shortly after we left with our cameras – the men forced their way onto the site and demanded that workers down tools. The Federation for Radical Economic Transformation represents a number of business forums nationwide. Spokesperson Sifiso Shezi claims the Federation is making a positive impact in bridging the divide between their members and contractors. SIFISO: our forums affiliate to us they've got a constitution. They are registered and therefore anything else that calls itself forum outside of that we we we we distance ourselves from them VO: While Shezi admits there’s been trial and error to their approach in the past, he insists the federation’s members are not thugs. MAC: I as an ordinary citizen was scared for my life. SIFISO: Well it's an isolated incident. And most of them there that are taking that shape I guess they fear they fall outside of the scope of our mandate. It's an element that // we need to isolate it and condemn it with all contempt that it deserves. VO: It is by no means an isolated incident. This is daily reality for contractors all over the country confirmed Mnisi. ROY: // in many areas that we experience these mafia tendencies. The contractors are black contractors the main contractors and subcontractors all black contractors. M28 VO: In some cases, the exploitation even extends to the very people they claim to represent explains Barnard. PETER: // when these forums come along they then take a cut or a percentage of the money that's generated meaning that the actual humans on site doing the work end up by earning less than they would have earned if they'd been employed directly. M6 VO: Shezi argues, forums are not unions and are there to make money. SIFISO: // just because it's black business it doesn't mean now we must we must take care off of the social element of the economy. We are there not to make money like every other business and we are not saying we we are not apologetic it's a capitalist system // M30 VO: Some forums have even taken it a step further – they don’t want jobs, they’ll simply settle for cold hard cash. UPSOUND CELLPHONE CLIPS – ASK FOR MONEY….peacefully. JAS: // it's either protection money or buyout and then they say well we'll leave your site and you can work with who you want and we won't bother you. MAC: What kind of money are we talking about. JAS Well anything from a few thousand to hundreds of thousands at one time M14 KAREN: // I mean the moment that you pay any of them back you are done. I mean I refused to pay protection money because otherwise how can I work M31 VO: It seems to be a lucrative income stream – with these rogue business forums even going up against each other. ROY: // even if you were to give them their demands tomorrow, another one comes and say OK you contracted with that one. It's not part of us. We are independent from them. You have to contract with us. It can't work and it's not working at all.M29 VO: Shezi also doesn’t feel things are working – he believes the current legislation simply cannot effectively address economic transformation – it needs to include the private sector too. SIFISO: // We need to be cognizant of the imbalances of the past // we are talking about people that have been colonized for centuries. People that have been given a certain type of education and all of a sudden you come and say we voted. We are equal. We can never be equal. Hence the that the legislation of 30 percent participation in government is not sufficient to transform the economy. MULTI2 M6 LINK: //CUT calling it economic transformation doesn’t justify thuggery… it’s criminal behavior that costs the country billions of rands in losses and negatively impacts on international investor perceptions – this is economic sabotage. WEBSTER: All these cases where the violently disrupt and over 2 billion Brain Project. [from middle of clip]// You cannot equate it to. A boy who has stolen a bar of chocolate in a supermarket // You need to deal with this matter should the prevention of organized crime // M15 VO: President Ramaposa promised action in his 2020 State of the Nation Address. UPSOUND SONA: “I have prioritised our response to the growing problem of criminal groups that extort money from construction and other businesses. Specialised units – bringing together SAPS and the National Prosecuting Authority – are mandated to combat these crimes of economic disruption. “ VO: While all parties agree that economic transformation is necessary, the execution is problematic and these disruptions are not ecomically sustainable. PETER: We can't have South African business growing at gunpointM8// If the will of the people is that there's not enough being done in the industry. Construction specifically for radical economic transformation. Then there has to be dealt with by the legislature. ROY: if we don't deal with this problem I am afraid we will see the collapse of the construction industry in South Africa. //. M17 // M18 // we will continue to see many people losing their jobs as a result of this so-called construction mafia // PROMO 1 VO: A series of attacks on construction projects by violent thugs known as the Construction Mafia, cripple the economy under the guise of radical economic transformation – costing the country billions. PROMO 2 VO: Construction sites are disrupted by so-called business forums demanding their cut in projects - they violently threaten workers and ruthlessly damage propety – is this economic transformation or mafia tactics at work? PROMO 3 VO: They’re known as the Construction Mafia – so-called businness forums brazenly intimidate and violently threaten construction companies around the country, demanding a cut of the profits. metadata.Summary: Corporate South Africa is under siege. Businesses are engulfed in wave after wave of illegal protest action often marred by violence, harm and the destruction of property. Construction sites across the country are brought to halt by local communities claiming to be Business Forums that demand their cut in projects – be it in the form of employment, sub-contracting or in some cases straight up cash. We investigate this alarming trend and the impact it has on the country’s economy.
metadata.Further information: WHAT’s THE STORY The so-called construction mafia has been disrupting construction projects countrywide, demanding that 30% of the project value be awarded to local companies. In some instances the groups, calling themselves business forums, seek control of the full 30%, with the aim of distributing jobs and contracts among local workers and business people themselves. But their demands are not always so idealistic – they want cash to go away. IT’s SPREADING ACROSS SA After leading a campaign of terror for many years in KwaZulu-Natal, have infiltrated Gauteng and laid siege to construction projects and mining companies all over the province and surrounding areas. FINANCIAL IMPACT The financial impact of these protests is catastrophic – no business can sustain the continuous onslaught of work stoppages, delays in completing works, threats and intimidation to management, and employees living in constant fear of their lives. In 2019 the construction mafia had disrupted and halted at least 78 projects worth a minimum of R25.5 billion. Illegal site disruptions caused listed construction and engineering group Aveng and European-based Strabag International to withdraw from an SA National Roads Agency (Sanral) project that forms part of the N2 Wild Coast Road Construction project, over fears for the safety of their employees. Armed gangs in March last year also halted construction on the R2.4 billion German oil storage investment project being built in Saldanha by JSE-listed construction group WBHO. THE MAFIA MO A mob of protestors is mobilised to demonstrate outside a construction site based on a concocted grievance mostly along the lines that the private company has flouted its statutory obligations – in other words, unproven allegations that the company hired labour or appointing sub-contractors from outside the local community. They get violent, they threaten staff and in some cases they resort to straight up extortion. WHO IS THIS MAFIA? The mob representatives pass themselves off as the (self-appointed) local chapter of a ‘business forum’, or community. FEDERATION FOR RADICAL ECONOMIC TRANSFORMATION (FFRET) FFRET represents at least 37 business forums which reportedly has more than 3 000 members. The organisation’s leader Malusi Zondi acknowledged to that most of these members are former criminals to other journalists. Zondi has said Ffret is working to professionalise the members and is organising itself in all provinces, adding that members shut down construction sites because they were robbed of their “fair share” (by contractors). NATIONAL TREASURY The situation had arisen due to local communities misunderstanding a National Treasury regulation about subcontracting that was implemented in April 2017. The Preferential Procurement Policy Framework Act, 5 of 2000 (PPPFA) requires, inter alia, bidders of projects to the value of R30 million or more to sub-contract at least 30% of the value of the contract to exempted micro enterprises (EMEs) or qualifying small business enterprises (QSEs) or a small business as defined in the National Small Business Act, 1996. The PPPFA applies to public enterprise (organs of state) only, and not to private business. There is no statutory obligation for a private business to allocate 30% of its works to contractors from the local area. There is no legal basis underpinning the protestors’ grievance. Treasury warned that organs of state that are using procurement preferences not provided for in the regulatory framework – including ring-fencing contracts for service providers and suppliers who live in a certain geographical area – are non-compliant and that such expenditure will be classified as having been irregularly incurred. THE PRESIDENT’s TAKE ON IT In 2018 Ramaphosa weighed in on the matter, the SABC reported. He was addressing business leaders in Pietermartizburg Ramaphosa referred to people who are hijacking policies and distorting radical economic transformation by disrupting sites and demanding 30% of the value of projects, describing these practices as “radical economic robbery” and calling for consequences. NOT JUST REGULAR CRIME The NPA agreed that the disruption of construction sites should not be dealt with as just a common criminal act but in terms of the Prevention of Organised Crime Act. SAPS have launched a dedicated unit under the Anti-Gang sector of Organised Crime in Gauteng to focus on these incidents. WHAT WE HAVE - We have videos of disruptions, threats of violence and demands made by the so-called construction mafia - We’ll have access to some these sites where there is current disruptions - We’re trying to get a specific person to confront who has been demanding cash INTERVIEWS - SA Forum of Civil Engineering Contractors (Safcec) CEO Webster Mfebe - Karen de Beer – Medium Size Contractor - Malusi Zondi – Federations for Radical Economic Transformation - Jas XXX – Security Contractor protecting sites - Informant – giving insight into the business forums - SAPS or LEGAL EXPERT – ACTING UNLAWFULLY, misunderstanding of National Treasury Regulation. - Confront with dodgy Business Forum
